item.title: A flat geodesic with a periodic asymptote
item.description: arXiv:2610.30707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a closed surface of genus $2$ with nonpositive Gaussian curvature and a complete nonperiodic flat geodesic asymptotic to a flat closed geodesic. The metric is of class $C^{3,1/3}$ and its curvature is of class $C^{1,1/3}$, but not $C^2$. Thus the periodic-asymptote obstruction for smooth surfaces does not extend to $C^1$ Gaussian curvature.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball
item.description: arXiv:2610.30771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball in hyperbolic space. We construct a locally constrained nonlinear curvature flow that preserves the $k$-th quermassintegral while monotonically increasing the $l$-th quermassintegral for any $(1\leq l<k\leq n)$. Using this flow, we establish a full family of the quermassintegral inequalities for horo-convex capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball with contact angle $\theta\in(0,\pi/2]$. Moreover, we weaken the horo-convexity to convexity and obtain the quermassintegral inequalities for convex capillary hypersurfaces between the $n$-th and $l$-th quermassintegrals.
item.dc:creator: Jinyu Guo, Liangjun Weng

item.title: Locally symmetric hypersurfaces in globally symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify locally symmetric hypersurfaces, understood in the intrinsic sense, in Riemannian globally symmetric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jihun Kim, Yuri Nikolayevsky, Ruy Tojeiro

item.title: Parametrization of ancient Ricci flows with smooth compact tangent shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ancient Ricci flows whose tangent flow at backward infinity is a smooth compact Ricci shrinker. After normalization, every nontrivial solution either converges exponentially or has polynomial decay governed by neutral directions. We recover the finite-dimensional parametrization of the exponentially convergent solutions and establish finite-order asymptotic expansions for all slowly convergent solutions. For principal slow solutions, we obtain a locally bijective finite-dimensional parametrization compatible with diffeomorphisms, parabolic rescaling, and time translation.
item.dc:creator: Yu Li

item.title: Complete conformal metrics of constant positive scalar curvature with prescribed isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.31058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with positive Yamabe constant. For any prescribed finite set $\Lambda\subset M$ containing at least two points, we construct a complete metric on $M\setminus\Lambda$, conformal to $g$, with scalar curvature $n(n-1)$. At each singularity, the local geometric term in the reduced action comes from the first nonzero homogeneous metric term of degree at most $(n-2)/2$ in finite conformal normal coordinates, or from the mass of the Green function metric when all such terms vanish. We completely solve Schoen's conjecture about singular Yamabe problem.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: On global Chern-Calabi flows on compact complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose the Chern-Calabi Flow for extremal metrics in conformal Hermitian geometry. After the existence of extremal metric, we consider the existence of global flows to the Chern-Calabi flows for extremal metrics on compact complex surfaces with Gauduchon metrics. To achieve this goal, we use the Adams inequality and the Gronwall inequality method to obtain fourth order derivative norm estimates. We also study the convergence of the global solution to the Chern-Calabi flow and its limit is the solution of the Chern-Calabi extremal metric problem. We propose a fourth order elliptic problem and derive the Bochner formula relevant to the elliptic estimates for the Chern-Calabi heat flow.
item.dc:creator: Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: A Chern-Weil theory for Lie groupoids with Cartan connections
item.description: arXiv:2610.31219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Chern-Weil theory to Lie groupoids carrying a Cartan connection. For a principal $(\Sigma, \omega)$-bundle $(P, {\theta})$ over $X$ we construct a map of differential graded algebras from an $\omega$-basic subcomplex of the Weil algebra of the Lie algebroid of $\Sigma$ to $\Omega^\bullet(X)$, whose map in cohomology does not depend on $\theta$. It recovers the classical Chern-Weil map for Lie groups, the Cartan model for action groupoids, and the characteristic classes of Cartan geometries for gauge groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Luca Accornero, Mateus de Melo, Ivan Struchiner

item.title: Three-orbifolds, positive scalar curvature and fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2610.31279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that closed Riemannian 3-orbifolds with positive scalar curvature have virtually free fundamental group. We also build a family of closed 3-orbifolds with free fundamental group of rank 2 which do not admit Riemannian metrics of positive scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Bessi\`eres, Sylvain Maillot, Ilaria Mondello, Thomas Richard

item.title: Convex-like Submanifolds, Caps and a Volume Comparison Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.31332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convex-like submanifolds in the Lorentz-Minkowski spaces are introduced in this paper as a natural and broad generalization of convex surfaces in the Euclidean space. Associated with such a convex-like submanifold in a Minkowski space, we define roofs (which resembles the supporting planes), caps (which are generated by the light rays in the normal bundle), and towers (which revives the notion of interior for such high codimensional objects). As a touchstone of this theory, a volume comparison theorem is proved, which is a non-trivial generalization of the obvious fact that among two nested convex surfaces, the outer one has larger volume. Finally we provide two important applications of this theorem.
item.dc:creator: Baichuan Hu, Xiang Ma, Dong Zhang

item.title: Lawlor's curvature criterion and topologically trivial area-minimizing hypercones of Hsiang type
item.description: arXiv:2610.31341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a closed embedded minimal hypersurface in a unit sphere, we show that the existence of a uniform vanishing angle in Lawlor's criterion suffices for its cone to minimize area. The normal-wedge condition follows from Howard's rolling theorem. We derive explicit curvature bounds and apply them to the reported Hsiang-Sterling curvature estimates for topologically trivial cones. The resulting area-minimizing cones give an affirmative answer to the existence question raised by Ilmanen and White (Camb. J. Math., 2015).
item.dc:creator: Hongbin Cui

item.title: A sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds and ADM mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.31343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g), n\geq 4$ be a close Einstein manifold with positive scalar curvature and $G$ be the Green function of the conformal Laplacian. The ADM mass of the asymptotically flat metric $\hat g:=G^{4/(n-2)} g$ is an important geometric invariant. When either $n=5$ or $n\geq 6$ with Weyl vanishing condition, we prove a mass formula, generalizing Gursky-Malchiodi's formula in dimension $4$. An important step is an extension of Viaclovsky's Green function expansion in higher dimensions. Next we prove a sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds. Finally we present two applications. First, we prove a mass gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. Second, for Collins-Sz\'ekelyhidi's family of Sasaki-Einstein metrics $g_i$ on $\mathbb{S}^5$ with volume going to zero, the sequence of the masses $m(\hat{g_i})$ blows up uniformly as $i\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Xuezhang Chen, Jiaxue Gan, Yalong Shi, Nan Wu

item.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mc Gowan

item.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exist exotic spheres with metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature in infinitely many dimensions: in every dimension $n\equiv3\pmod4$ with $n\geq11$ and $n\not\equiv255\pmod{256}$. Previously, every known closed simply connected manifold of positive sectional curvature in a dimension above $24$ was diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space. The spheres we consider are certain homotopy spheres arising as quotients of special $S^3$-$S^3$ bundles introduced by Speran\c{c}a. These homotopy spheres are determined by an orthogonal representation $\rho$ of $S^3$ and an $S^3$-conjugation-equivariant map $\beta$, and are denoted $\Sigma_{\rho,\beta}$. By recent constructions, such spheres admit Riemannian metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature. In this paper we consider the spheres $\Sigma_{\rho_b,\beta}$ of dimension $4b+3$, $b\geq2$, where $\rho_b$ is the representation of $S^3$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathbb{H}^b$ by left multiplication on the second summand. For these spheres, we show that the Eells-Kuiper invariant is the product of an integer $k(\beta)$ depending only on $\beta$ and a rational number $r_b$ given by one coefficient of a power series built from the $\hat A$- and $L$-genera. We then show that, for every $b\geq2$ with $b\not\equiv63\pmod{64}$, there is a map $\beta$ for which the Eells-Kuiper invariant does not vanish, and thus the corresponding sphere is exotic. A computer calculation also gives the dimensions $n\equiv255\pmod{256}$ below $2^{16}$.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Galaz-Garc\'ia

item.title: Collapsed translating solitons with planar wings
item.description: arXiv:2610.31669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study complete embedded translating solitons in R^3 with finite genus and finite entropy. We prove that such collapsed translators whose wings are all of planar type (in a weak topological sense) must be vertical flat planes. In particular, this implies the non-existence result for gluing and doubling constructions involving planes that was conjectured in (14) and announced in (9) as an application of the authors' techniques, under weaker assumptions than previous rigidity results by Khan and Lynch-Tinaglia in (17,19,20). A key ingredient is a sharp new a priori decay estimate in the exterior problem for the horizontal graphical translator equation, showing that bounded solutions to the nonlinear equation, and their gradients, are controlled by multiples of the Green's function of the linear drift Laplacian, regardless of the size of the given L^\infty data. Combined with a graphical description of the infinite ends and the Neves-Tian flux identity, this yields the main rigidity result. As another application, we obtain a full classification of collapsed embedded finite-genus translators of entropy lambda < 3.
item.dc:creator: Eddygledson Souza Gama, Francisco Mart\'in, Niels Martin M{\o}ller

item.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.30288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Niklas Garner, Martijn Kool, Jan Manschot, Yuuji Tanaka

item.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.30395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Louis

item.title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.30464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
item.dc:creator: Keith Burns, Tomas Gedeon, Yuping Ruan

item.title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{\lambda,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_\mu$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohu Nie

item.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.31191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.
item.dc:creator: Mich\`ele Levi

item.title: Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.31270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive K\"ahler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.31497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.
item.dc:creator: Andreas H\"oring, Vladimir Lazi\'c, Christian Lehn

item.title: A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
item.description: arXiv:2610.31584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee, Kui Li, Juncheng Wei

item.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends I: Holomorphicity and Uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2504.02282v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We show that any complete, oriented, immersed minimal surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with finite total curvature and genus $1$, and having these three ends, must be $J$-holomorphic for some almost complex structure $J$. If the surface is also embedded and has at least $8$ symmetries, we prove that its symmetry group has order $8$ or $12$. In each case the surface is uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.
item.dc:creator: Jaehoon Lee, Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Local Models for Special K\"ahler Metric Singularities Along the Discriminant Locus of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Hitchin Base
item.description: arXiv:2601.03761v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Freed (arXiv:hep-th/9712042) formulated the theory of special K\"ahler structures. In particular, the regular part of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Hitchin base $\mathcal{B}$ carries such a structure, and the associated metric $\omega_{\mathrm{SK}}$ develops singularities near the discriminant locus $\mathcal{D}\subset\mathcal{B}$. Baraglia--Huang (arXiv:1707.04975) showed that its Taylor expansion at regular points can be computed by topological recursion, and Hitchin (arXiv:1712.09928) later constructed integrable subsystems over smooth strata of $\mathcal{D}$ parametrizing spectral curves with only nodal singularities; these strata carry induced special K\"ahler structures. We show that near such strata, the special K\"ahler metric on $\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{D}$ exhibits logarithmic asymptotics in transverse directions, whereas its tangential part converges to a metric on the stratum that agrees with the one induced by Hitchin's subsystems. We also prove that the induced metric on every radial complex line through the origin and a point of such a stratum is flat with cone angle $\pi$ at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxi Huang, Shuo Wang, Bin Xu

item.title: Translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2601.14193v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a series of papers, Weil initiated the investigation of translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies, which include as prime examples Federer's curvature measures. In this paper, we continue this line of research by introducing new tools to study curvature measures. Our main results suggest that the space of curvature measures, which is graded by degree and parity, is highly structured: We conjecture that each graded component has length at most $2$ as a representation of the general linear group, and we prove this in degrees $0$ and $n-2$. Beyond this conjectural picture, our methods yield a characterization of Federer's curvature measures under weaker assumptions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Adv. Math. 503 (2026), part C, Paper No. 111275
item.dc:creator: Jakob Schuhmacher, Thomas Wannerer

item.title: Capillary minimal slicing and scalar curvature rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2602.21071v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop minimal slicing via capillary hypersurfaces to understand scalar curvature metric on manifolds bounded below with boundary. In particular, in dimension $4$, we prove following comparison and rigidity statement: given a compact Riemannian $4$-manifold $(M^4,g)$ with a mean convex boundary whose boundary is diffeomorphic to boundary of a connected convex domain in $\mathbb R^4$, if the scalar curvature is non-negative and the scaled mean curvature comparison holds along the boundary, then $M$ is isometric to the Euclidean domain. Moreover, we prove a comparison and rigidity result of manifolds with Listing type scaling invariant scalar and mean curvature comparison : $R g \ge -12 g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$ and $\hat{H}^{2} g \ge \hat{H}_{0} g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$, where $\hat{H}$ is a shifted mean curvature depending on the scale of manifold. This proves the traced version of Gromov's conjecture on comparison and rigidity of hyperbolic convex domains
item.dc:creator: Dongyeong Ko, Xuan Yao

item.title: Classification of Smooth Alignable Voss Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.17501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Alignable nets are grid structures that can collapse to a planar strip. This property simplifies on-site assembly and enables compact transport and storage. These structures are then deployed by a scissor motion at vertices in a desired location. In this article, we classify all non-developable surfaces supporting an alignable net that additionally have the geodesic-conjugate net property, namely, the alignable Voss surfaces. Using the surface elements and adapted frames, we show that these surfaces arise as rotation fields of either helicoidal pseudospherical surfaces or Amsler surfaces, resulting in two distinct classes. The first class consists of helicoidal Voss surfaces. Exploiting this helicoidal structure, we combine a kinematic interpretation with the Bour family to derive explicit immersion formulas depending on the isometric deformation and alignability parameters. Furthermore, we examine several subclasses and an extension of this result in detail. In particular, we study the notable case of infinitely many geodesic-conjugate nets on a helicoid and provide a kinematic explanation for why this phenomenon appears in computations. For the second class, we obtain the classification at the level of the fundamental forms and show that they correspond to certain $3$-parameter families of non-helicoidal intrinsic surfaces of revolution. These families are governed by general Painleve III solutions including both regular and nonregular solutions. Finally, a surprising feature of this class is that its members support geodesic isothermal-conjugate nets absent from Eisenhart's classification of the aforementioned nets, thereby identifying a missing case in that classification.
item.dc:creator: Arvin Rasoulzadeh

item.title: On weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2605.08796v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The notion of weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics extends the classical notion of Calabi's extremal K\"ahler metrics, but includes many well-studied objects in K\"ahler geometry such as K\"ahler-Ricci solitons and Sasaki-Einstein metrics. In this paper, after explaining how this notion grew out, we will try to survey recent works concerning the YTD conjecture on weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Akito Futaki

item.title: A min-max gap characterization of minimal foliations on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2605.12428v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend an energy introduced by Mather to the setting of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory and obtain a parametric, higher-dimensional analogue of Mather's variational barrier theory for twist maps and geodesics on tori. We use this energy to establish several criteria for the existence of foliations of the $n$-torus by minimal hypersurfaces. We show that for a generic metric, whenever a lamination by area-minimizing hypersurfaces of the $n$-torus contains a gap, there exists a minimal hypersurface inside the gap that is not area-minimizing. This hypersurface is a higher-dimensional analogue of the secondary minimax orbit appearing in Aubry-Mather theory.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: Jacobian estimates and geometric inequalities under intermediate Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.13690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Jacobian estimate underlying both the Heintze--Karcher comparison and the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci method for submanifolds of arbitrary codimension. The estimate retains the contributions of ambient curvature along geodesics emanating from the submanifold and requires no curvature sign assumption. As applications, we obtain a quantitative Fenchel--Willmore inequality with explicit curvature remainders under nonnegative $n$-intermediate Ricci curvature, Michael--Simon Sobolev and isoperimetric inequalities under nonnegative $(n-1)$-intermediate Ricci curvature, and corresponding extensions under quadratic curvature decay. In each result, the required intermediate Ricci curvature condition depends only on the dimension of the submanifold and is independent of its codimension.
item.dc:creator: Kwok-Kun Kwong, Jihye Lee, Fabio Ricci

item.title: Spin and scalar curvature on punctured four manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.37948v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a closed spin four-manifold with nonzero signature, even after being punctured along a finite graph, does not admit a complete metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature. We also show that this implies Schoen's conjecture on $L^{\infty}$-metrics with non-negative scalar curvature for these manifolds. This is in contrast to higher dimensions. A key new observation, which could be of independent interest, is that Gromov's $\mu$-bubbles are a convenient class of boundaries for the APS boundary value problem for the Dirac operator.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kumar, Boyu Zhang

item.title: Clifford Actions and the Algebra of Double Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.04428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $V$ be an oriented Euclidean vector space and let $\D(V)=\Lambda V^*\otimes\Lambda V^*$ be the algebra of double forms. The two exterior factors carry natural factorwise exterior and interior multiplication operators and therefore two commuting Clifford actions. The central result of the paper is an intrinsic realization of these Clifford actions inside Greub's composition algebra. For $a\in V^*$ we introduce the inhomogeneous double form \[ \chi_a=((1\otimes a)-(a\otimes1))e^g, \] prove that the $\chi_a$ satisfy the Clifford relations for the composition product, and establish the exact regular-action formulas \[ C_R(a)\omega=\chi_a\circ\omega, \qquad C_L(a)\omega=-\omega\circ\chi_a. \] For $h\in\D^{1,1}$ this yields a canonical four-component decomposition of the coupled left--right Clifford action into exterior multiplication, double contraction and two generalized Bianchi operators. For the metric double form $g$ these four operators generate two commuting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ actions. The construction extends canonically to arbitrary bidegree. In bidegree $(2,2)$ its degree-preserving component admits a direct comparison with the double-form extension of the sharp product: for every $R\in\D^{2,2}$, \[ \Gamma_{1,1}(R)(\omega)=\frac14R\#\omega. \] The point of this identity is not a new definition of $R\#$, which is already constructed from Clifford commutators, but the fact that it appears canonically as the central homogeneous component of the higher left--right Clifford transform. As an application, the algebraic quadratic map $\mathcal Q(R)=-\frac14R\#R$ satisfies \[ \mathcal Q(R)=-\Gamma_{1,1}(R)R, \] and its linearization at $R$ is the operator $-2\Gamma_{1,1}(R)$. For curvature tensors this is the sharp contribution to the Ricci-flow reaction term.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Belkhirat

item.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.10132v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.13848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in Euclidean 3-space with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from a periodic solution of a Riccati equation.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Banks, Mohammad Ghomi, Hongda Qiu, Matteo Raffaelli

item.title: Robust Tangent Space Estimation via Laplacian Eigenvector Gradient Orthogonalization
item.description: arXiv:2510.02308v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Estimating the tangent spaces of a data manifold is a fundamental problem in geometric data analysis. The standard approach, Local Principal Component Analysis (LPCA), struggles in high-noise settings due to a critical trade-off in choosing the neighborhood size. Selecting an optimal size requires prior knowledge of the geometric and noise characteristics of the data that are often unavailable. In this paper, we propose a spectral method, Laplacian Eigenvector Gradient Orthogonalization (LEGO), that utilizes the global structure of the data to guide local tangent space estimation. Instead of relying solely on local neighborhoods, LEGO estimates the tangent space at each data point by orthogonalizing the gradients of low-frequency eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian. We provide two theoretical justifications of our method. First, a differential geometric analysis on the tubular neighborhood of a manifold shows that gradients of the low-frequency Neumann eigenfunctions of the tube align closely with the manifold's tangent bundle, while an eigenfunction with high gradient in directions orthogonal to the manifold lies deeper in the spectrum. Second, a random matrix theoretic analysis also demonstrates that low-frequency eigenvectors are robust to sub-Gaussian noise. These results allow us to derive the asymptotic scaling and stability of the estimated eigenvector gradients. Numerical experiments demonstrate that LEGO yields tangent space estimates that are significantly more robust to noise than those from LPCA, resulting in marked improvements in downstream tasks such as manifold learning, boundary detection, and local intrinsic dimension estimation.
item.dc:creator: Dhruv Kohli, Sawyer J. Robertson, Gal Mishne, Alexander Cloninger

item.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
item.description: arXiv:2603.27252v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.
item.dc:creator: Jinrong Hu, Yingxiang Hu, Bo Yang

item.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $\Delta_pu+ \Delta_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.23624v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Biqiang Zhao

item.title: An infinity-categorical TQFT from instantons
item.description: arXiv:2606.29902v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we lift the instanton TQFT from ordinary categories to the $\infty$-categorical setting by constructing a functor $CI:\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}\longrightarrow\mathsf{D}$ from an $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ for instantons to an $\infty$-derived category $\mathsf{D}$ of $2$-periodic chain complexes. The construction of $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ is a modification of the $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{Bord}_4$ introduced by Lurie and by Calaque--Scheimbauer using complete Segal spaces. The target $\infty$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is obtained via the dg nerve of the dg category of $2$-periodic chain complexes of finitely presented projective $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. The information encoded by the functor $CI$ was already developed by Kronheimer--Mrowka using families of metrics on cobordisms. Our reinterpretation in terms of $\infty$-categories conceptually simplifies the construction of the hypercube complexes underlying the link spectral sequence. This viewpoint also clarifies hyperbox complexes and compression in Manolescu--Ozsv\'{a}th's work, and possible $A_\infty$-structures, especially their signs and higher coherence. In addition, we lift the generalized cap product $\mu$-operators in instanton Floer homology to the chain level and construct explicit homotopies and higher homotopies establishing the commutativity of multiple $\mu$-operators in even degrees.
item.dc:creator: Fan Ye

item.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2607.17362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Cueca, Florian Dorsch, Reyer Sjamaar, Chenchang Zhu

item.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
item.description: arXiv:2608.03575v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.
item.dc:creator: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou

item.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.31089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental K\"ahler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact K\"ahler manifold admits such Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of K\"ahler classes on higher compactifications.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Trusiani
